newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso sinks 7.05 vs dollar amid emergency.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso sinks 7.05 vs dollar amid emergency.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed down 7.05 at 1,023.6 against the dollar Tuesday as the economic emergency decreed by the government sent a wave of speculation through the markets, interbank traders said.
The peso crashed to an intraday low of 1,040 early in the session, its lowest since Sept 13, as banks speculated on the possible effects of the emergency measures.
Traders reported 340 trades worth a total $168 million. The peso hit an intraday high of 1,021, and the session average was 1,027.87 pesos per dollar.

Dealers reported little demand for greenbacks outside banks and financial insitutions. Some private exporters took advantage of the favorable rate to pump small amounts of export earnings into the market, brokers said.
"Today's movement was completely down to the economic emergency decree. The rate rose early on a wave of speculation," a dealer said.

Traders, however, said they believed the economic emergency measures so far announced, which include slashing back foreign debt and taxing public and private companies that look abroad for loans, would help push down the value of the peso.
The government is looking for a mininimum devaluation of 15 percent in the value of the peso against the dollar in 1997.
